title_en: Throwing a Brick to Attract Jade
full_text_zh:
[P1] 抛砖引玉

[P2] 绞国是春秋时期的一个小国，它的邻国是强大的楚国。楚国一点一点地吞并了周围的小国家。公元前700年，楚国终于要攻打绞国了。绞国国君收到消息，立即下令：‘快关城门！’绞国的城门又厚又重，四五个士兵才能推动。守城的士兵收到命令，赶紧将城门关得严严实实的。

[P3] 楚军来了！
怎么办？
怎么办？
镇定
虽然三万楚军驻扎在绞国的南城门外，
但绞国国君还是很镇定。绞国兵少，
出城迎战没有胜算。
但是，楚军远道而来，肯定想速战速决。
只要绞国能坚守城池半年，楚军
自然会知难而退！

[P4] 绞国国君早就料到楚国会来攻打，已经做好了一切准备。
绞国周围是连绵不绝的群山，山上林深树密，楚军攻不进来；护城河挖得又宽又深，还从山上引来了活水，楚军渡不过来；城墙修得又高又厚，楚军的攻城器也砸不烂；仓库里堆满了粮食，够城里的士兵和百姓吃上半年。

[P5] 第二天，楚国大军攻城了！
如果楚军攻进城里，绞国人就要亡国了。谁也不愿意国破家亡，绞国士兵一个个拼死守城。
一天下来，楚军死伤无数，却连护城河也没有攻过去。天黑后，楚军只好鸣金收兵。

[P6] 晚上，绞国的城墙上燃起了熊熊的篝火，照得城头一片大亮。
这时是寒冬，守城的士兵正好可以一边取暖一边防守，楚军也不敢来偷袭。

[P7] 天气越来越冷，攻城更难了，楚国的伤兵每天都在增加。堂堂楚国，攻打一个小小的绞国，却几个月都没有打下来，楚王心里又气愤又着急。
半夜，雪越下越大，护城河结了一层薄冰。

[P8] 城里的绞国国君呢，这时候也遇到了一个大难题：没柴了！
绞国人以前都是从山上砍柴烧，现在城门紧闭，出不去了。但是，城里的人每天还得烧水、烧饭、取暖，守城的士兵还得在城墙上燃篝火。储存的木柴很快就烧光了。

[P9] "拆门窗！"绞国国君一声令下，士兵们就来到老百姓家里，拆了他们的门和窗，还顺手收走了他们的干柴。冬天睡在没有门窗的房子里，许多百姓都冻伤了。绞国国君左右为难，再这样下去，即使防住了楚军，城里也会乱起来呀！

[P10] "禀告国君，有士兵出城抢柴了！" 绞国国君听到报告，大吃一惊！
原来，守城的将士没了柴草，夜间不但要挨冻，还要担心楚军来偷袭。他们站在城墙上，远远地盯着城外的山林，便发现......

[P11] 楚军每天都会派老弱残兵去山上砍柴！一些绞军士兵就悄悄地从北城门出去，抢了他们的柴草。
“楚军有没有派人保护？”绞国国君急忙问。
士兵得意地回答：“没有。我们抢了他们的柴草就走，他们都不敢追呢！”
绞国国君一想到城内柴草紧缺，便没有禁止士兵们出城抢柴。

[P12] 楚王听说，绞军经常抢掠楚军砍柴的士兵，心中十分恼火。楚王想派一队强壮的士兵去保护他们。这时，莫敖屈瑕灵机一动，想出了一个办法。他劝楚王说：‘绞国这么小，没什么聪明人。咱们不用派强兵去保护砍柴兵，反而要让他们天天去砍柴，把绞军都引出来。’

[P13] 接下来的几天，天空乌云密布，北风呼啸，雪花飘飘，河面都结了冰。因为接连几天抢了不少柴草，出城的绞军越来越多。有一次，绞军竟然抓到了三十个楚国的砍柴兵。屈瑕见绞国人已经上了钩，就要准备收“竿”了。

[P14] 第二天，楚军没有攻城。绞军以为他们已经疲惫不堪，没有力气打仗了。于是，上百名绞军将士争着抢着出了北城门，赶着抓到的楚兵上山去砍柴。他们砍了很多柴，正背着准备回去时......

[P15] 突然，林中冲出无数楚军，把他们全都抓了起来。
天快黑的时候，守城的将士们见砍柴的士兵回来了，急忙打开城门。没想到，那一百多名士兵蜂拥而上，杀掉了守兵守将，然后一声呼哨，大批楚军像潮水一般冲进了城。
绞国国君战败被俘，无奈之下，只好签订了盟约，向楚国投降。

[P16] 钓鱼需要用鱼饵，先让鱼儿尝一点甜头，它才会上钩；抛出去的鱼饵就像砖头，钓上来的却是肥硕的鱼儿，犹如美玉。打仗时也一样，先让敌人占一点便宜，敌人才会钻进圈套。这样的计策，就叫“抛砖引玉”。
full_text_en:
[P1] Throwing a brick to attract a jade

[P2] Jianguo was a small state during the Spring and Autumn period, with the powerful state of Chu as its neighbor. Chu gradually annexed surrounding small states. In 700 BC, Chu finally decided to attack Jianguo. Upon receiving the news, the king of Jianguo immediately ordered: 'Close the city gate quickly!' The city gate of Jianguo was thick and heavy, requiring four or five soldiers to push it. The soldiers guarding the city received the order and quickly shut the gate tightly.

[P3] The Chu army is here!
What should we do?
What should we do?
Calm down
Although 30,000 Chu soldiers are stationed outside the southern gate of Jiao State,
the King of Jiao remains calm. Jiao has few troops,
and fighting outside the city would be hopeless.
However, the Chu army came from afar and surely wants a quick victory.
If Jiao can hold out for half a year, the Chu army
will naturally retreat!

[P4] The king of Jiao had long anticipated that Chu would attack, and had already made all necessary preparations.
The area around Jiao was surrounded by endless mountains, with dense forests on the slopes, making it impossible for Chu's army to advance; the moat was dug wide and deep, with fresh water brought down from the mountains, preventing Chu's army from crossing; the city walls were built high and thick, so that Chu's siege weapons could not break them; the granaries were filled with food, enough to feed the soldiers and civilians in the city for half a year.

[P5] The next day, the Chu army launched an attack on the city!
If the Chu soldiers broke into the city, the people of Jiao would face national destruction. No one wanted to see their country fall and their homes destroyed, so the Jiao soldiers fought to the death to defend their city.
By the end of the day, the Chu army had suffered countless casualties, yet they still couldn't even cross the moat. After dark, the Chu army had no choice but to sound the retreat and withdraw.

[P6] At night, the walls of Jiao State were lit by roaring bonfires, illuminating the city's ramparts.
It was winter, and the defending soldiers could warm themselves while guarding, making it too risky for the Chu army to launch a surprise attack.

[P7] The weather was getting colder and colder, making the siege even harder. The number of wounded soldiers in Chu was increasing every day. Such a mighty Chu, attacking a tiny state of Jiao, had failed to capture it after months. King Chu was both angry and anxious.
In the middle of the night, the snow fell harder and harder, and a thin layer of ice formed on the moat.

[P8] What about the king of Jiao State inside the city? He now faced a big problem: no firewood!
People from Jiao State used to chop wood from the mountains for burning, but now the city gates were closed and they couldn't go out. However, people inside the city still needed to boil water, cook meals, and keep warm every day, and the soldiers defending the city still had to light bonfires on the city walls. The stored firewood was quickly burned up.

[P9] "Break down doors and windows!" The King of Jiao gave the order. Soldiers went to the homes of the common people, tore down their doors and windows, and took away their firewood. In winter, sleeping in houses without doors or windows, many people got frostbite. The King of Jiao was torn between choices. If things continued like this, even if they defended against the Chu army, chaos would break out in the city!

[P10] "Your Majesty, some soldiers have gone out of the city to steal firewood!" The King of Jiao, upon hearing the report, was greatly shocked!
It turned out that the defending soldiers had run out of firewood. At night, they not only had to endure the cold, but also feared a surprise attack by the Chu army. Standing on the city walls, they stared far into the forests outside the city, and then discovered......

[P11] The Chu army sent old and weak soldiers to chop firewood in the mountains every day! Some soldiers of Jiao secretly went out from the northern gate and stole their firewood.
"Did the Chu army send anyone to protect them?" the King of Jiao asked anxiously.
The soldier proudly replied, "No. We took their firewood and left; they didn't dare to chase us!"
Thinking of the severe shortage of firewood inside the city, the King of Jiao decided not to forbid his soldiers from going out to steal firewood.

[P12] King Chu heard that the army of Jiao often raided the Chu soldiers who were chopping firewood, and he became very angry. He wanted to send a squad of strong soldiers to protect them. At this moment, Mo Ao Qu Xia had a sudden idea and came up with a plan. He advised King Chu: 'Jiao is so small, it has no clever people. We don't need to send strong troops to protect the woodcutters. Instead, we should let them go out to chop wood every day, luring the Jiao army out.'

[P13] In the following days, the sky was filled with dark clouds, the north wind howled, snowflakes drifted down, and the river surface had frozen. Because they had stolen a lot of firewood in recent days, more and more Jiao soldiers were going out of the city. Once, the Jiao army even captured thirty Chu soldiers who were gathering firewood. Qu Xia saw that the Jiao people had taken the bait, and was about to prepare to reel in the 'rod'.

[P14] The next day, the Chu army did not attack the city. The Jiao army thought they were already exhausted and had no strength left to fight. So, hundreds of Jiao soldiers rushed out of the northern gate, leading the captured Chu soldiers up the mountain to chop firewood. They chopped a lot of wood and were just about to carry it back when......

[P15] Suddenly, countless Chu soldiers burst out from the forest and captured them all.
As dusk approached, the defending soldiers saw the woodcutters returning and hurriedly opened the city gate. Unexpectedly, the over one hundred soldiers surged forward, killed the guards and commanders, then gave a single whistle, and a large force of Chu troops rushed into the city like a tide.
The King of Jiao was defeated and captured. With no choice, he had to sign a treaty and surrender to Chu.

[P16] Fishing requires bait. First, let the fish taste a little sweetness, and it will bite. The bait thrown out is like a brick, but what is caught is a plump fish, as precious as jade. In war, it's the same: first let the enemy gain a small advantage, and then they will fall into the trap. This strategy is called 'throwing a brick to attract jade.'
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页标题为“抛砖引玉”，配图是一位身穿橙色长袍、头戴木枷、双手被锁链束缚的男子，正趴在地上哭泣，表情痛苦，似乎在表达某种牺牲或引出更珍贵事物的寓意。
[P2] 本页讲述了春秋时期小国绞国面临强敌楚国进攻的紧急情况，国君下令紧闭城门，士兵们合力将厚重的城门关严实，以抵御外敌。
[P3] 面对三万楚军压境，绞国士兵惊慌失措，而国君却镇定自若，分析敌我形势，决定坚守城池，以时间拖垮远道而来的楚军。
[P4] 本页描述了绞国国君为抵御楚国进攻所做的周密准备，包括利用地形、加固城防、挖掘护城河、储备粮食等，展现了其未雨绸缪的智慧。
[P5] 楚国大军攻城，绞国士兵拼死抵抗，楚军伤亡惨重却未能攻破城池，最终在天黑后撤兵。
[P6] 夜晚，绞国城墙上点燃了熊熊篝火，士兵们在寒风中取暖并守卫城池，楚军因畏惧而不敢偷袭。
[P7] 本页描绘了楚国围攻绞国的困境：天气转冷，攻城愈发困难，楚军伤亡增加，楚王又气又急；同时，半夜大雪纷飞，护城河结冰，进一步加剧了攻城难度。
[P8] 本页描述了绞国在城门紧闭、无法外出砍柴的情况下，面临木柴耗尽的困境，国君和百姓因缺乏燃料而陷入困境。
[P9] 绞国国君为抵御楚军，下令拆百姓门窗取柴，导致百姓冻伤，国君为此感到左右为难，担心城内会因此混乱。
[P10] 一名士兵向绞国国君报告有士兵出城抢柴，国君大惊。原来守城将士因柴草耗尽，夜间既受冻又担心楚军偷袭，站在城墙上远望城外山林，发现了某种情况。
[P11] 绞国士兵发现楚军每天派老弱士兵上山砍柴，便趁机出城抢夺柴草，且楚军不敢追击。绞国国君得知后，因城内柴草紧缺，决定不禁止士兵出城抢柴。
[P12] 楚王因绞军劫掠砍柴士兵而恼怒，莫敖屈瑕献计，建议让楚军士兵天天去砍柴，以引诱绞军出城，从而创造战机。
[P13] 天气寒冷，河面结冰，绞军因柴草紧缺频繁出城抢夺楚军砍柴兵，一次竟抓到三十人。屈瑕见计策奏效，准备收网。
[P14] 绞军误以为楚军疲惫，便带领俘虏的楚兵出城上山砍柴，砍得许多柴火，正准备返回时，画面戛然而止。
[P15] 楚军趁绞军出城砍柴时突袭，一举攻破城门，俘虏绞国国君，迫使绞国投降。
[P16] 本页通过钓鱼的比喻，解释了“抛砖引玉”的计策，即先让对方占小便宜，诱使其上当，从而实现战略目的。
